notes: Focused v1.7.4 correctness regressions for facts corrected after the October 2026 freshness audit, checked against tagged upstream sources (bubbletea v2.1.0, huh v2.0.3, lipgloss v2.0.6, ratatui 0.30.2, ratatui-textarea 0.9.3, tokio select! semantics, Ink 8.0.0 release notes, the Node.js release schedule, Typer 0.26.0 release notes, pytest-textual-snapshot 1.1.0 metadata, Claude Code fullscreen docs, the Copilot CLI changelog, and lazygit's go.mod). The ratatui-select-reader-ends and ratatui-ctrl-c-raw-mode cases grade sample fixes that land with the reference sample checks (#42). Assertions define the grading rubric; improvement claims require a recorded harness run against one immutable skill hash. Status (2026-10-13): rubric-only. The v1.8.0 evidence round (#43) ran the v170, v171, v173, and v180 sets but not this one; no run is recorded under evals/results/ or scheduled.

evals.name: huh-v2-embedding
evals.prompt: I'm embedding a huh v2 form inside my Bubble Tea v2 model. My model has a `form *huh.Form` field. What should my Update and View look like so the form receives messages?
assertions: Type-asserts the huh.Model returned by form.Update back to *huh.Form instead of assigning it directly to the *huh.Form field
Returns or batches the tea.Cmd that form.Update produces
Composes the form's string view into the parent's tea.View rather than returning the string as the view
Requests the terminal background color from the parent program (Huh does not request it itself) and forwards the resulting message to the form

evals.name: lipgloss-v2-printing
evals.prompt: My non-interactive Go CLI uses Lipgloss v2 styles and prints with fmt.Println(style.Render(msg)). Is that fine when stdout is piped or NO_COLOR is set?
assertions: Says Lipgloss v2 Render always emits full-color escape sequences regardless of the output
Recommends lipgloss.Println, Sprint, or Fprint, which detect the output's color profile and downsample or strip color for pipes and NO_COLOR
Does not recommend lipgloss.SetColorProfile or a renderer-based fix, which were removed in v2

evals.name: ratatui-textarea-crate
evals.prompt: Which crate should I use for a multi-line text editor widget with vim/emacs-style bindings in a Ratatui 0.30 app?
assertions: Recommends ratatui-textarea, maintained under the ratatui organization
Says tui-textarea 0.7 depends on ratatui 0.29 and is unmaintained, so it does not fit a Ratatui 0.30 app
Warns against pulling in a second crossterm version, or imports crossterm through ratatui::crossterm

evals.name: ratatui-select-reader-ends
evals.prompt: My Ratatui app's Tokio loop is `loop { tokio::select! { Some(event) = rx.recv() => app.handle(event), _ = tick.tick() => app.on_tick() } if app.quit { break } }`, with a separate task reading crossterm events into the channel. What happens if that reader task exits?
assertions: Explains that when rx.recv() returns None the Some(event) pattern fails, select! disables that branch, and the loop keeps ticking with no input
Notes the user cannot quit because Ctrl+C arrives as a key event in raw mode, not as SIGINT
Fixes it by matching the None case and breaking out or returning an error
Restores the terminal on that exit path

evals.name: ratatui-ctrl-c-raw-mode
evals.prompt: My Ratatui app quits on `q`. Users report that Ctrl+C does nothing. Why, and what should the key handling be?
assertions: Explains that raw mode clears ISIG, so Ctrl+C is delivered as a key event instead of SIGINT
Handles KeyCode::Char('c') with the CONTROL modifier as quit or cancel, alongside q and optionally Esc
Acts only on KeyEventKind::Press so key-release events are ignored

evals.name: ink8-new-project
evals.prompt: We're starting a new Ink CLI today. Which Ink, React, and Node versions should we target, and can I still read the terminal width from useStdout().stdout.columns?
assertions: Names Ink 8 as the current major, requiring Node 22 or newer and React 19.3 or newer
Recommends Node 22 or 24 and does not recommend Node 20, which reached end-of-life in April 2026
Says Ink 8 types stdout as a generic Node stream, so stdout.columns no longer type-checks, and recommends useWindowSize()
Mentions at least one other Ink 8 breaking change, such as number-only minWidth and maxWidth or useInput dropping unrecognized terminal sequences

evals.name: cjs-require-esm
evals.prompt: Our CLI is still CommonJS on Node 22. Do we have to pin chalk 4 and an old Ink to keep using require()?
assertions: Says Node 22.12 and later (and 20.19) can require() synchronous ES modules, so ESM-only packages such as chalk and commander no longer force old pins
Says Ink cannot be loaded with require() because its dependency graph uses top-level await, which fails with ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE
Recommends await import('ink') or a bundler for Ink in a CommonJS program

evals.name: typer-vendored-click
evals.prompt: I want to add Trogon (or another Click plug-in) to my Typer app so users get a TUI for the CLI. How do I wire it up?
assertions: Says Typer 0.26 and later vendor Click instead of depending on it, so Click plug-ins and extracting the Click app are no longer supported
Says Trogon breaks with Typer 0.26 or later and is unmaintained
Offers a concrete path, such as pinning typer below 0.26, writing the CLI with Click directly, or building the TUI separately

evals.name: ai-chat-rendering-tradeoff
evals.prompt: I'm building an AI chat client for the terminal with streaming responses. Should I keep the transcript inline with Ink's <Static>, the way Claude Code does it, or use the alternate screen?
assertions: Corrects the premise: Claude Code's fullscreen renderer uses the alternate screen and renders only visible messages, and GitHub Copilot CLI uses the alternate screen, while Gemini CLI stays inline
Explains that inline rendering keeps the terminal's scrollback, search, and copy, but its cost grows with the transcript
Explains that an alternate-screen renderer keeps memory flat and avoids flicker but must rebuild search, copy, and export to scrollback
Recommends keeping an inline or plain fallback for screen readers or users who prefer scrollback

evals.name: gocui-new-app
evals.prompt: I'm building a lazygit-style multi-panel Go TUI. Should I use gocui like lazygit does?
assertions: Says lazygit copied its gocui fork into its own repository (pkg/gocui) on tcell v3, so there is no maintained upstream gocui to depend on
Recommends Bubble Tea, or tview for widget-heavy apps, for a new project
Does not recommend adding jesseduffield/gocui as a dependency

evals.name: textual-snapshot-pytest9
evals.prompt: After upgrading to pytest 9, my Textual snapshot tests started writing .raw files instead of SVGs and my async Pilot tests error out. What changed?
assertions: Says pytest-textual-snapshot 1.1.0 pins syrupy 4.8, which requires pytest below 9, so pip falls back to 1.0.0
Recommends pinning pytest below 9 for snapshot suites until the plugin is updated
Says async Textual tests need pytest-asyncio with asyncio_mode = "auto" or an explicit asyncio marker
